label: text
text: CREW OF "NORGE" SAFE.

label: text
text: Nome: May 16.

label: text
text: The population, who donned gala dresses, prepared a monster demonstration to welcome the "Norge." They were disappointed to hear that Amundsen had ten-minated his trans-Polar flight at Teller.

label: text
text: Now York, May 16.

label: text
text: The crew of the "Norge" and safe. The adership is deflated and will be shipped to the United States from Teller immediately.

label: text

label: text
text: EARLIER NEWS

label: text
text: The Norge has arrived at Teller Alaska.

label: text
text:
Washington, May 15.
The Nome Army Radio Station was heard communicating with the Norge this morning.

label: text
text: New York, May 15.

label: text
text: The Norge landed at Teller, which is a small "trudingg, post in the reindeer centre, amid the silent snows. The population of the place is 200, mainly Esquimaux. Teller possesses a deep inlet and one of the calmest harbours in that region. Williamburg (Virginia). May 15.

label: text
text: "Trans-Polar flight successful. Respectful greetings." This was the text of a wireless message from Ellsworth, second in command of the Norge, to President Coolidge. The President wirelessed back "Message received. Hearty congratulations."

label: text
text: The news of the Norge's "safe arrival spread like wildfire throughout the country. Newspapers immediately published special editions, and the streets were decked with flags and thronged with enthusiastic crowds.

label: text
text: There was great excitement in Parliament when the news was announced. The Norwegian Legations at Washington and Rome were instructed to congratulate the American and Italian Governments.

label: text
text: Rome. May 16.

label: text
text: Delirious demonstrations of joy took place when it was learned the Norge had safely landed in Alaska. The streets and public buildings were beflagged and bells were peel-ed in the capital.

label: text
text: Signora Noble, weeping with joy, appeared on the balcony, and thanked the enthusiastic crowd; The announcement in the Chamber of the Norge's arrival was received with prolonged cheering, the Deputies standing.

label: text
text: Late Saturday Cubles

label: text
text: The Government radio station here is in touch with wireless stations in the Far North, including stations at the mouth of the Mackenzie river and Herschell island but all report that they have searched the air fruitlessly for any report from the airship. "Norge."

label: text
text: One of the most plausible theories to explain the continued absence of news of the "Norge" in advanced by Mr. Hankon Hammer, who was associated with Amundsen's Polar expedition plans in 1924. He suggests that the al-ship is resting at Wainwright inlet, 70.40 north and 160 degrees west of Northern Alaska, the old Amundsen base, where there is a cache, gasolene, and other supplies.

label: text
text: Mr. Hammer adds that the high mountain ranges in the neighbourhood would afford a good shelter from an impending storm; whilst plenty of Eskimos are available to assist the "Norge" to land.

label: text
text: The airship "Norge," containing Amundsen, and his party of explorers, was reported missing on May 14, a message from Oslo stating that huge crowds watched the progress of the airship on May 18.

label: paragraph_title
text: POLISH REVOLT:

label: text
text: SEQUEL TO PILSUDSKI'S

label: text
text: Warsaw, May 16.

label: text
text: Following an interview with Marshall Pillsudski, M. Ratav, Marshall in the Diet, who will constitutionally temporarily assume the Presidency of the Republic, a Government of experts, mostly officials, has been formed until a National Assembly, composed of the Diet and Senate, elects a new President.

label: text
text: Professor Bartel is Premier; Marshal Pilsudski goes to the War Office, and M. Tialeski, ex-Ambassador at Rome, becomes Foreign Minister.

label: text
text: The new Premier Professor Chsimir Bartel, is also Minister of Railways. He obtained his engineering degree at Munich.

label: text
text: Professor Bartel and M. Ratay have both issued statements urging the necessity of a return to the constitutional position as soon as possible.

label: text
text: It is reported that General Sikorski, Commanding the Army Corps at Lwow, has placed himself under the command of Marshall Pilsudski.

label: text
text: As the result of an appeal by Professor Bartel to the railwaymen in the evening terminated the strike declared on Wednesday as a protest against M. Witos's Government.

label: text
text: It is reported from Warsaw that the President, M. Wojciechowski, and the Prime Minister, M. Witos, resigned after an all-night conference.

label: text
text: Eondon, May 15.

label: text
text: A message from Warsaw confirms that the rising has ended in a triumph for General Pilsudski, who has taken over the Presidency, and is arranging a new Cabinet... Garrisons concentrated at Waraw have been instructed to return to their districts.

label: text

label: text
text:
At an extraordinary meeting of the Singapore Cold Storage Coy., Ltd., Mr. J. Lonie presiding, a resolution was passed that each 100,000 shares of ten dollars be divided into five shares of two dollars each and that the capital of the Company be increased to $2,000,000 by the creation of half a million new shares of two dollars and that the Directors be authorised to create a debenture stock of a nominal amount of $750,000 bearing interest at seven per cent. The chairman stated that the increase of capital would enable the Company to purchase the Strats Ice Company.

label: paragraph_title
text: MERCiless CANTONESE

label: text
text: 10 FORTS DESTROYED

label: text
text: Systematic lawlessness by some Cantonese bandits is described in a report from Canton.

label: text
text: Of the Foong Chuen district, the report says:—For years the neighbouring villages have been pillaged and burnt. Several hundred bandits occupied the 8rd section, Sheung Li. Over 1,000 villagers were kidnapped and murdered and several hundred cottages were rezed to the ground.

label: text
text: In the middle of last year the bandit chiefs of the Tsat Sing Ngaam (Seven Star Cave) united with others numbering over 3,000 strong, fully equipped with arms, suddenly attacked the 5th section. The Militia Corps were unable to resist them. Over 3,000 houses and over 10 forts were set on fire, several hundred villagers were killed or kidnapped, and 2,000 cows and other property were taken. The total loss was over $200,000.

label: text
text: On May 7 the outlaws captured the busiest market centre of the district. All the merchants suffered heavily. Villagers who escaped with their lives became homeless or were compelled to starve.

label: text
text: Nearly half of the Foong Chuen district is in the hands of the bandits. Communications have been suspended. The bandits call themselves soldiers of a certain Independent Regiment. (says the report) and publicly announced that they would capture the 4th section and attack the city. If they succeed it will mean they will control the strategic point of the two Kwang provinces. At the same time the Sheung Li bandits are also active. The 4th section is now surrounded on four sides by bandits. The people of various places have stopped business. It is reported that the magistrate, who is on the point of going away, telegraphed for help, but, up till now no troops have arrived.

label: text
text: An appeal has been sent to the Canton Government by the Protection Corps; asking for immediate help.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE CANNON CASE

label: text
text: The case in which the master of a Yaumati engineering shop stands charged with manufacturing cannon was again before Mr. J. H. B. Nihill at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning when Det.-Inspector Pincott asked for one week's further remand.

label: text
text: Mr. W. B. Hind, for the defence, mentioned that he was investigating the possibility of the cannon being used in the manufacture of peanut oil and we would probably ask for another adjournment at the end of one week.

label: paragraph_title
text: MANILA CUSTOMS COLLECTIONS FOR APRIL

label: text
text: Showing an increase of P94,449,55 over the gross customs collections for all ports of entry during April of last year, the collections for all ports, excepting Legaspl, for April, 1926, amounted to P1,764,338.05. The customs collections last year amounted to P1,669,888.50.

label: text
text: The gross internal revenue collections for all ports in April of this year amounted to P515,411,84 as compared with P392,349.39 collected during the same period in 1925, or an increase of P123,062.45.

label: text
text: Professor Shellshear, of the University, has reported the theft of a microscope valued at $80 from a class room.

label: text
text: A Chinese's hroff in the employment of Messrs. Alex; Ross and Company is reported to have absconded with $500 collected on behalf of the firm.

label: text
text: Following a quarrel with her parents, a young Chinese woman attempted to commit suicide at West Point on Saturday by jumping into the harbour. She was rescued by boat people.

label: text
text: The manager of a theatrical troupe at the Taiping Theatre stated in a report to the police on Saturday that some person has stolen a box containing money, clothing and jewellery to the value of about $115.

label: text
text: A Portuguese named E. M. R. Remedios was fined $1 at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning for committing a nuisance in a public place. It was stated that he was in the habit of visiting the Police Station during the weekend looking for lodging and had previously been in Court and at the House of Detention.
